name: Narendra Modi
role: Prime Minister of India (2014–present); Chief Minister of Gujarat (2001–2014)
summary: Modi leads a nationalist, state-led development agenda that pairs market opening and private enterprise in some sectors with large public investment, welfare delivery and self-reliance in energy, defence and technology. He stresses national heritage and unity, a single civil code and constitutional order, and attacks dynastic politics and corruption; his government ended Jammu and Kashmir's special status and took a hard line on Pakistan.

dynastic-succession.rationale: In his 2024 Independence Day speech he said dynastic politics causes significant harm to Indian democracy and the country and politics must be freed from it; he repeats the attack on 'family first' parties in Parliament.

office-by-exam.rationale: He announced the end of interviews for lower non-gazetted central posts (Groups B, C, D) from 1 January 2016, saying interviews bred corruption and recommendation-seeking, so those posts rest on written tests.

region-keeps-system.rationale: He led the 2019 revocation of Article 370, calling it a denial of due rights that had given the state secessionism and corruption, and in 2025 praised 'the removal of the wall of Article 370' and 'One Nation, One Constitution'.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: His government had Parliament withdraw Jammu and Kashmir's special powers and downgrade it to a Union Territory in 2019; he defended the Union Territory arrangement as an administrative choice, saying it may not need to continue in Jammu and Kashmir.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He calls corruption a termite that has shattered the common man's faith in the system and says he has waged a war on it, though his charges are aimed mostly at the opposition and earlier governments.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He calls the 1975 Emergency a sin of 'murdering the Constitution' in which the country became a prison, so he rejects suspending ordinary protections in that case; he has not addressed other emergencies.

return-lost-territory.rationale: In his 12 May 2025 address he set out as India's stated policy that any talks with Pakistan would be only on terrorism and on Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, treating that territory as India's to be taken up.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The 2003 Gujarat anti-conversion law passed under him as chief minister, but no source opened shows him driving or speaking for it, so his own position is not known.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Mixed: his Pink Revolution rhetoric and the 2011 Gujarat slaughter ban point one way, his central government's support for meat-processing plants the other.

limit-population.rationale: In his 2019 Independence Day speech he warned of a 'population explosion', called a small family a form of patriotism and said central and state governments should act, mainly through awareness.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: He describes the nation as heir to a heritage thousands of years old from which it draws energy, and asks the world to understand India's values and thousands of years of history.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: He says the strength of India's culture lies in its diversity and calls that diversity its great inheritance and pride; he speaks of cultural and linguistic diversity rather than racial diversity.

local-production.rationale: He urges every citizen to make 'Vocal for Local' and Swadeshi a life mantra and to buy only products made in India; this is a national rather than a local-region preference.

cut-welfare.rationale: His speeches stress expanding social security cover from 25 crore people before 2014 to 100 crore and free health cover to the elderly, and he calls it saturation of welfare delivery; he voices no dependency argument against it.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: He announced from the Red Fort a next generation of GST reforms in which taxes on goods needed by the common man would be reduced substantially and everyday items become cheaper.

free-trade.rationale: He presents the free trade agreements signed with nearly 40 countries since 2014 as a huge opportunity for Indian producers to reach world markets.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He lists state-led missions as his own policy: a state semiconductor manufacturing programme with plants now running, the Mission Green Hydrogen, and 85,000 crore rupees for the Samudra Manthan offshore exploration mission.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He called the old ban on exploring 99 per cent of India's coastal area 'poverty of thought', opened it as a 'Go-Ahead Area' and committed 85,000 crore rupees to Samudra Manthan to find new domestic oil and gas.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He cites the SHANTI Act and a target of 100 gigawatts of nuclear power by 2047 with five new reactors this decade, and in 2025 said ten new reactors were progressing.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He points to a tangible record on climate, including 500 GW of renewables by 2030 and net-zero railways by 2030, and a 50 per cent clean energy target met in 2025, but stresses meeting targets and energy self-reliance rather than drastic measures.

limit-growth.rationale: He sets growth targets (a developed India by 2047) and presents clean energy as compatible with them, never proposing to limit growth for the environment.

accelerate-technology.rationale: He tells the nation that emerging technologies (AI, quantum, space, robotics) must be led by India and announces training one crore youths in AI, and says reform must not be held back by older laws and systems.

military-superiority.rationale: He announced the Sudarshan Chakra Mission to build a national security shield by 2035 that would neutralize attacks and hit back many times harder, and reports defence production up nearly fourfold in twelve years.
